nature: PROSPECTIVE held-out cohort. Generated from a fixed seed and frozen by git blob SHA before any Spark, Coq or SQLite execution of these queries.
checker: check2 / check2_sound (QueryProofDeepRewrite.v over QueryProofDeepGuard.v), unchanged from V16 apart from report fields
spark: official pyspark==4.2.0 wheel with the disposable AST trace overlay
unit: one effective rule event (old != new) in the captured Catalyst trace

definitions.ACCEPTED: the kernel-checked Example `check2 old new = true` compiles
definitions.REJECTED: the kernel computes `check2 old new = false` (also kernel-checked)
definitions.UNKNOWN: the trusted printer cannot express the event (Unsupported); counts as NOT accepted
definitions.coverage(rule): ACCEPTED / all effective events of that rule, UNKNOWN included in the denominator
definitions.mutant: a JSON-level adversarial variant of an ACCEPTED event, from the families in run_v15.py (IFFC: 6 families; other rules: 4 families). Every family is semantically wrong for some database by construction
definitions.mutant ACCEPTED: kernel says check2 = true on the mutant; this is a safety failure

H1_zero_mutants_accepted.statement: No mutant of any accepted event is accepted, for either rule.

H4_no_other_rule_accepted.statement: No effective event of any other rule is accepted (any such acceptance would still be sound by check2_sound, but it would be unexpected).

H5_oracle_agreement.statement: Spark and independent SQLite result bags agree on every query both engines execute (pipeline sanity, not a checker test).

expected_unknown_sources: aliased projections and aggregates under pushed filters
reporting: All counts are reported whether or not thresholds are met. Failures and infrastructure reruns stay on record. UNKNOWN is never counted as accepted.
